contexts.text: The pleasant things of taste. Signified.
Taste, like the other bodily senses, corresponds to celestial and spiritual things.
The soul gives to the body to appetize food, and also to relish it: foods are introduced by the delight of appetite and of relish; thus by external good.
To appetite and relish correspond the longing and affection of knowing truth.
Therefore wisdom, or to be wise, is so called from relish.
He could not discern anything interior...
The predominance of good is represented in the flavour in the grapes.
Its appearing delightful in the external form, is signified by, its taste being sweet as honey ()... But the internal sense is signified by the bitter taste. Explained.
They said that to them useful food is savoury.
The taste of the manna was like... ()... Taste is predicated of the delights which are of good, because it corresponds to the delight of wisdom.
Compared to foods unclean to the sight, but savoury.
Salt makes food savoury...
They are accepted as genuine truths, because they savour of good.
He is in a life which savours of the world.
These simulations... savour of justice and judgment. CL 281.
How a substance tastes...
For then man has a sense of the good in the truth.
Relish and taste = the affection of knowing and being wise.
Hence, in languages, relish, and to savour, are predicated of the perception of a Thing; hence also comes sapientia.
Its taste = perception...
